back_translation: Oh how the city that was once crowded with people now sits all alone! She who was great among the nations has become like a widow. She who was a princess among the provinces has been put to forced labor.
She weeps bitterly in the night, tears wet upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers she has no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh servitude. She dwells among the nations but finds no resting place. All her pursuers have overtaken her in her distress.
The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the appointed feasts. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan; her young maidens grieve, and she herself is in great bitterness.

Her adversaries have become her masters; her enemies are at ease, because the LORD has made her grieve for her many transgressions. Her little children have been driven away as captives before the adversary.
All splendor has departed from the Daughter of Zion. Her princes are like deer that find no pasture; they flee exhausted before the pursuer.

In the days of her affliction and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the precious things that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into the adversary's hand and no one helped her, her adversaries looked at her and laughed at her collapse.
Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become an unclean thing. All who once honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns her face away.
Her uncleanness clings to her skirts; she gave no thought to her end. Her fall is therefore astonishing; she has no one to comfort her. “O LORD, look upon my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed.”
The adversary stretched out his hand and seized all her precious things. She saw the nations invade her sanctuary — those You had commanded not to enter Your assembly.
All her people groan as they search for bread. They trade their treasures for food to sustain life. “O LORD, look and consider, for I am despised.”
All you who pass by, does this mean nothing to you? Look and see: is there any pain like my pain, which has fallen on me, which the LORD made me suffer in the day of His fierce anger?
He sent fire from on high into my bones, and it prevailed over them. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He made me desolate, faint all day long.

My transgressions have been bound into a yoke; His hand wove them together; they lie draped upon my neck. My strength has been broken down. The Lord has given me into the hands of those I cannot withstand.
The Lord has cast aside all the mighty warriors in my midst. He has summoned an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden the Virgin Daughter of Judah as in a winepress.
For these things I weep; my eyes, my eyes stream with tears. For the comforter who would revive my spirit is far away. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.

Zion stretches out both her hands, but she has no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that his neighbors become his adversaries. Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.
The LORD is righteous, for I rebelled against His word. Hear, all you peoples, and look at my pain: my maidens and my young men have gone into captivity.
I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they sought food to sustain their lives.

See, O LORD, for I am in deep distress. My inward parts are in turmoil; my heart is overturned within me, for I have been very rebellious. Outside the sword bereaves; inside the house there is only death.

People have heard my groaning, but I have no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my calamity; they rejoice that You have done it. Bring the day You have proclaimed, so that they may become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before You, and deal with them as You have dealt with me for all my transgressions. For my groans are many, and my heart is faint.
